gaps.text: In-line measurement of Broth temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of NIR and fluorescence spectra into one matrix with block scaling, from a combined probe at the same spot. Acquisition must be synchronised to a common time step, and each block needs its own calibration and drift checks. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the extra channel is dropped.)
Which offline reference methods suit this broth, and at what frequency, is not addressed by the supplied sources.
A quantitative relationship between optical density and cell mass for this broth is not given in the sources.

items.finding: The source notes that OH-band temperature sensitivity is a severe drawback for aqueous NIR and MIR measurement, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This supports including broth temperature monitoring or control and checking temperature drift when interpreting optical signals.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The quote comes from a review on biopharmaceutical downstream processing and does not validate an in-line temperature sensor in yeast broth or define its placement or calibration.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: Low-level fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into one new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform building a fused NIR-plus-fluorescence matrix, but synchronisation and block scaling still need separate design and checks.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The review is general PAT data fusion, not a yeast fermentation or a combined NIR/fluorescence probe, and it does not report performance on held-out runs.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: The source advises evaluating each dataset's contribution and complementarity before fusing multiple sources.
items.how_it_applies: This supports comparing the fused model against the best single method and dropping an extra channel if it does not add value.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: It is a general recommendation, not a tested NIR/fluorescence fusion in this broth, and it gives no threshold for when a fused model has beaten a single method.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: The source says NIR spectra are harder to interpret than conventional analyses such as chromatography and UV-VIS because absorption bands overlap.
items.how_it_applies: This could justify including conventional reference analyses alongside NIR to help interpret overlapping bands, but it does not identify broth-specific methods or sampling frequency.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The context is pharmaceutical unit operations, not yeast fermentation broth, and the quote does not establish that these methods are offline or suitable at any frequency.

citation.quote: However, a disadvantage of NIRS is that it is more difficult to interpret a signal than by using conventional analysis methods, such as chromatography, ultraviolet/visible (UV-VIS) light, and others, because the absorption bands overlap due to spectral complexity.
citation.label: E03 ¶13
